Team — thanks for taking the loop today. Satish finished his onsite last evening (backend + systems + pairing). Quick ask to get us to a hire/no-hire decision: please add your scorecard by EOD Monday and flag any explicit blocking concerns. I pulled his resume into the Drive (attached) and dropped a clean scorecard template there as well.

Summary notes from interviews (high level):
- Backend system design: solid architecture, latency-aware tradeoffs.
- Scaling experience: has led multi-region cache invalidation work at previous company.
- Pairing: showed pragmatic debugging approach, but one of the interviewers noted a few unclear abstractions.

If you disagree with the rubric or want to propose a score uplift/downshift, call it out explicitly with reason — we may need a quick tiebreak.

Folks — saw the scorecards, thanks. I put a 7 overall with a specific callout: Satish has great design instincts but on the pairing exercise he relied on a private helper function pattern that would make it hard for an unfamiliar on-call engineer to reason about the state machine. That increases cognitive debt.

If we want to get to hire without a separate loop: propose a 1-hour technical follow-up with team members from runtime (Avery + me) focusing on the failure-mode questions and the helper-function abstraction. If he demonstrates clearer abstractions we can consider hire with small onboarding checkpoints. If not, we should table.

Laura
Director, Engineering
